optional_capability_rule: Cases with gate null require separate leaf tasks and gates before implementation/qualification; not added as earlier-stage prerequisites

cases.title: Short write and sync uncertainty
cases.acceptance: Inject partial payload/trailer writes and sync failure with both surviving and lost bytes; no success before sync, uncertain attempted commit fences writers

cases.title: ACK, ABORT, UNKNOWN external history
cases.acceptance: Controller records typed row/index/catalog history outside candidate; production reopen preserves ACK, excludes explicit ABORT and allows only whole UNKNOWN commits. Validate one history across reopen, including reads of recovered UNKNOWN effects and subsequent commits; do not independently discard such effects on a later restart.

cases.title: Tail versus required corruption
cases.acceptance: Truncate active tail under declared crash model, corrupt sealed/interior frames and remove referenced data; only allowed incomplete tail ignored; required corruption errors. Include full-length torn body/trailer writes; record the qualified fault profile and retain fail-closed behavior when ambiguous. Freeze separate RECOVER_OK and REJECT_CORRUPTION vectors, including torn unacknowledged final frames arising from normal crash. A rejection must preserve source bytes and expose no normal queries or new ACKs; it is not successful automatic recovery.

cases.title: Repeated recovery crash
cases.acceptance: Crash during decode/apply/verify/checkpoint recovery, then restart twice from retained source; no duplicate mutation or skipped redo. Also recover an old permitted incomplete tail, establish the next writer epoch, ACK a new transaction, crash again and preserve both old and new acknowledged history. Add process-only crash retaining a complete unsynced old frame in OS cache, STABILIZE of old files/namespaces, new-epoch ACK, then power-loss model discarding remaining volatile state. Omission of prior-prefix stabilization must be detected. Failed/uncertain stabilization blocks WRITER selection and READY. For power loss before or partway through STABILIZE, freeze each surviving image and its expected result in advance: valid retained prefixes recover, full-length torn unsynced frames reject as corruption. RECOVER_OK at every subsequent RESUME cut requires the complete stabilization barrier first; never reclassify a result after execution.

cases.title: Statement and transaction effects
cases.acceptance: Multi-row failure, cancel and epoch conflicts restore statement/private state without exposing partial row/index changes

cases.title: Concurrent exact-cut checkpoint
cases.acceptance: Update same row chunks while checkpointing pinned C; compare all roots to independent history exactly at C. Capture root C, replay anchor offset/prefix digest, allocator high-water and pins together; rotate and commit while immutable checkpoint files are built.

cases.title: Every manifest and selector crash cut
cases.acceptance: Fault file sync, rename and directory sync before/after manifest and CURRENT publication; choose complete old/new state; corrupt selector fails closed. Cover CURRENT-only checkpoint selection serialized with commit/rotation/Retiring, actual WRITER tip preservation, old/new closure union on uncertain selection, and corrupt WRITER rejection.

cases.title: Early reclaim mutant
cases.acceptance: Delete old replay WAL before CURRENT directory sync in mutant; independent restore must detect ACK loss. Also delete the anchor segment or a required epoch link in a mutant; missing required files must never be mistaken for intentionally pruned pre-anchor history.

cases.title: Fallback chain completeness
cases.acceptance: Retained previous manifest must retain all subsequent commit/payload/page dependencies; no automatic old-generation open with missing chain. Reclaim only before every retained anchor and reopen using both current and previous; cover two anchors in one segment, empty genesis/new epoch, fallback CURRENT reselection with previous absent, and subsequent checkpoint/restart without re-registering damaged current.

cases.title: Pin versus GC race
cases.acceptance: Concurrent reader/backup pin and generation retirement; no delete-after-check race, bounded orphan cleanup after crash. Retiring approval uses coordinator then ledger; selector uncertainty prevents new Retiring. Prior-approved deletes remain outside all old/new closures; restart rebuilds ledger before GC.

cases.title: Empty-environment exact-cut restore
cases.acceptance: Restore copied checkpoint closure in separate empty owned directory with independent row/index/catalog checks and interrupted restore. Restore without source WAL by binding state C to a fresh timeline/base-q=C segment and new local manifest/selectors; then ACK a new write and restart. Interrupted creation with missing required selectors/files is rejected as incomplete; a complete surviving selection must reopen normally. Never silently open a partial database.

cases.title: Disk row/index/catalog atomicity
cases.acceptance: Fault WAL/undo/status/page/DWB/FILEMAP/commit boundaries with steal/no-force; row/index/catalog all-or-none logical visibility, ACK preservation and UNKNOWN fencing; commit need not force data pages

cases.title: Undo and dirty-page retention with repeated recovery
cases.acceptance: Retain snapshot/rollback/version links, allocator generations, current/previous WAL floors and selected pending DWB images. Reclaim begin WAL only after complete undo/status/allocation redo closure; rollback still succeeds. Durably select recovery WRITER before first CLR; second restart must discover it.

cases.title: Bounded DISK recovery
cases.acceptance: Data/index/locator/allocation inventory each >=4x buffer, bounded ATT/runtime DPT and streaming redo. Normal reopen avoids full cold data scan; separate offline full integrity audit and independent history required. Fixed recovery/flush workspace and no proportional disk spill.

cases.title: Serializable group validation
cases.acceptance: Actual threads plus controlled schedules for absent/range/unique/catalog conflicts; batch intra-dependencies; stale root replacement mutant rejected

cases.title: Group commit crash and ACK ordering
cases.acceptance: Whole group framing/sync/publication, lost response, failed group without partial adoption, no abort after possible commit

cases.title: One payload lane lost
cases.acceptance: Valid commit references two lane fragments and COW pages; missing any dependency gives explicit startup error, never partial success

cases.title: Reservation hole
cases.acceptance: Later write finishes before earlier reserved range; contiguous frontier never jumps hole; max-offset mutant rejected

cases.title: Commit order and stream epoch
cases.acceptance: Payload physical order differs from q; validate commit prefix and topology; reject missing group, wrong DB/timeline, stale reused segment

cases.title: Prepared payload older than checkpoint tail
cases.acceptance: Delayed transaction later commits using old offset; GC must retain active reservation and referenced payload

cases.title: Parallel recovery dependencies
cases.acceptance: Decode/apply schedule changes with same-key/global-index/catalog/row-move conflicts; equal independent serial history and atomic publication

cases.title: Stalled lane and disk full
cases.acceptance: Bounded queue/pins, slow sync and ENOSPC; admission rejects before commit where possible, UNKNOWN fence otherwise; required data never deleted

cases.title: All earlier same-major recovery formats required by the central version policy
cases.acceptance: For releases and source baselines designated by version-compatibility-policy.json: old checkpoint/WAL/backup into new engine including skipped minors, failed conversion and L0 to L2 transition; new writes survive restart. For distributions outside the compatibility domain, record the policy-defined not-required status; current-build recovery remains mandatory. No prior applicable baseline is N/A, not PASS.
cases.applicability: customer-delivery qualification only; previous internal distributions excluded

cases.title: PITR archive object closure
cases.acceptance: At the selected storage profile, missing required backup/redo/namespace dependencies reject restore; complete target-boundary closure restores into a new timeline. DEV3 uses base backup plus redo, not old root-only COW object rules.

cases.title: Replication consumer retention
cases.acceptance: Slow consumer pins correct ranges/objects; explicit resync transition; physical refs or logical row-delta path actually present

cases.title: Bounded persistent codec
cases.acceptance: Unknown version/type, malicious lengths, truncation, checksum and compression expansion rejected without unbounded allocation

cases.title: Commit-before-payload mutant
cases.acceptance: Persist commit without one payload sync then crash with that payload lost; mutant must be rejected as unsafe

cases.title: Like-for-like throughput latency and RTO
cases.acceptance: L0/L1/L2 on pinned hardware/FS, same durable ACK/isolation, actor/hotspot/size/media/checkpoint axes; TPS,p99,aborts,CPU,bytes,amplification,RTO and budgets; SLO acceptance must be set before qualification

variant_policy: Every required variant inherits NOT_RUN from its case; freeze exact fixtures, cuts and expected outcome before execution. Corruption/I/O rejection passes do not count as successful reopen or power-loss recovery.

profile_application.DEV2: K0-K5 cases retain their private/COW expectations
profile_application.DEV3: RC-T12-14 plus DS01-06; shared ACK/UNKNOWN/fault rules retained; fuzzy checkpoint, mutable-page redo/undo and offline backup use DEV3 variants
profile_application.L1_L2: legacy proposal only, NOT_RUN; storage-aware redesign required before applying to DEV3
